summary: Petition under Section 79 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Regulations 41 and 42 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 (as amended) seeking approval of intra-group transfer of shareholding of Petitioner No.1, AMPIN Energy C&I Thirteen Private Limited (AMPIN C&I 13), from Petitioner No.2, AMPIN C&I Private Limited (AMPIN C&I) to Petitioner No.3, AMPIN Energy Utility Private Limited (AEUPL). The present Petition has been filed by the Petitioners, AMPIN Energy C&I Thirteen Private Limited (AMPIN C&I 13), AMPIN C&I Private Limited (AMPIN C&I), and AMPIN Energy Utility Private Limited (AEUPL) seeking the following reliefs: 2. The instant Petition has been filed _inter alia_ seeking relaxation of Regulation 11A 3. The matter was admitted on 7.4.2026, and notice was issued to the Respondent to file its reply. The Respondent has filed its reply. 4. The matter was further listed for hearing on 22.5.2026. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioners submitted that since the Detailed Procedure under Regulation 11A(6)(c) of the GNA Regulations had not been notified at the time of filing of the instant Petition, the Petitioners had approached CTUIL _vide_ letter dated 3.3.2026 for approval of the transaction. However, since no reply was received from CTUIL, the Petitioners were constrained to file the present Petition. The learned counsel further submitted that AETPL holds 51% shareholding in both AMPIN C&I and AEUPL, thereby exercising ‘control’ over both entities in terms of Section 2(27) of the Companies Act, 2013. Accordingly, AMPIN C&I 13 will continue to remain a step-down subsidiary of AETPL, and AETPL will continue to exercise ‘control’ over AMPIN C&I 13. According to the Petitioners, there is no change in ‘control’ in the present transaction, and the rigours of Regulation 11A(6) of the GNA Regulations are not attracted. The learned counsel further clarified that the Petitioners are not seeking any advance ruling from the Commission, nor are they seeking to dilute, relax, or circumvent the promoter/control requirements under Regulation 11A(6). The learned counsel further submitted that in terms of Regulation 11A(6) and CTUIL’s letter dated 24.4.2026, it is clear that CTUIL’s permission is not required in cases where there is no change in ‘control’, therefore, the Commission may dispose of the present Petition, holding that there is no change in control and in line with CTUIL’s letter dated 24.4.2026. The learned counsel for the Respondent/CTUIL _inter alia_ submitted that the Petition seeks a general, forwardlooking pronouncement on how Regulation 11A(6) ought to apply to a class of intragroup restructurings, so as to secure advance clarity for the Petitioners’ proposed transaction structure. The Petition, in substance, seeks an advance ruling on intra-group transfers under Regulation 11A(6), and not redress against any identified _lis inter_ parties. The Petition substantially invites an advisory jurisdiction which the statute does grantee itself, and if it does, only then does the connectivity grantee, such as the AMPIN C&I 13 herein, require approaching CTUIL for its approval. In response, the learned counsel for the Petitioners submitted that the Commission may dispose of the present Petition by taking on record his submission that, in terms of the CTUIL’s letter dated 24.4.2026 and the reply dated 15.5.2026, there is no change in control in the present case, attracting the requirement of CTUIL’s prior approval under Regulation 11A(6). The learned counsel sought liberty to file his memo of arguments/ additional note of arguments to this effect. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties and the representative of CTUIL, the Commission permitted the Petitioner to file its additional note of argument/memo of arguments. 5. The Petitioners, _vide_ its Memo dated 8.6.2026, have submitted that CTUIL`s prior approval under Regulation 11A(6) is required only if the proposed transaction results in any ‘change in control’ of the connectivity grantee. However, in the present case, there is no change in control, since the ultimate parent company, i.e., AMPIN Energy Transition Pvt. Ltd, would continue to exercise control over the connectivity grantee even after the proposed transfer from Petitioner No. 2 to Petitioner No. 3, both of which are subsidiaries of AETPL. Therefore, neither Regulation 11A(6) nor Clause 16 of the Detailed Procedure would be applicable in the present case. The Petitioners have further submitted that CTUIL, in its letter dated 24.4.2026, addressed to all connectivity grantees in the Northern Region, has itself admitted and clarified that in cases where there is no ‘Change in Control’, prior approval of CTUIL is not required under Regulation 11A(6). The Petitioners have further submitted that CTUIL, in its reply, also has alluded to the fact that Regulation 11A(6) prescribes that the original promoter/ group that applies for and is granted connectivity must retain control over the Connectivity Grantee up to the COD. 6. Accordingly, in light of the CTUIL`s stand in its letter dated 24.4.2026 and reply in the instant Petition, the Petitioners have sought permission for withdrawal of the present Petition with liberty to approach the Commission in case there is any change in the position communicated by CTUIL. 7. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties and the Petitioner’s Memo dated 8.6.2026, the Petitioners are permitted to withdraw the present Petition.
